header:
Date: 2025-11-07
Time: 11:00 PT / 19:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Jiro Tanaka (Redwood CSM), Carlos Mendes (Talam Head of ML), Erin Zhou (Talam Infra Lead), Priya Singh (Talam Security), Ben Lowe (Talam Procurement)
summary: Renewal discussion focused on capacity uplift and adding EU region with private VPC options. Customer is evaluating cost vs latency tradeoffs and needs SOC2/KMS clarifications before contract extension. Agreed to run benchmarks and share pricing addendum. Pilot kickoff conditional on meeting latency SLOs.
topics: renewal timeline, dedicated capacity uplift, EU region onboarding, VPC/private deployment options, SOC 2 & KMS questions, benchmark plan, pricing and SOW next steps
transcript:
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanna make sure this call covers the renewal numbers and the multi-region plan, so I'll hand over to Carlos for quick context.
00:18 Carlos: Thanks Maya. Quick background, we hit about 150 million tokens a month now, spikes to 10k reqs/min during peak, primarily US, but EU traffic is growing - we need lower RTT for EU customers. We're on hosted right now, looking at dedicated or private VPC to tame cost and guarantee latencies.
00:42 Liam: Got it — thanks. Quick clarifying Q, are you seeing most of the EU traffic originate from specific countries (like DE/FR/UK) or is it broad? That'll affect region placement.
00:55 Erin: Mostly Germany and Netherlands, a little FR. We tried a CDN-like split but the latency for generative flows still hurts.
01:10 Priya: From security side we need to confirm data residency and KMS integration. Our lawyers also asked about audit logs and retention — SOC two pointers would help.
01:28 Maya: Yep we can do SOC 2 docs; I'll loop in our security pack. Quick note on pricing: you mentioned 150M tokens — want to confirm expected growth for the renewal term?
01:40 Carlos: Planning for 2x next year, so 300M tokens, and burst headroom for new features. We want committed baseline + burst.
01:52 Jiro: Onboarding note — if you go dedicated you get reserved GPU pools and a predictable throughput SLA; private gives VPC and key control. Either path supports model pinning.
02:10 Ben: Procurement here — timeline: we need legal review, sign-off by end of November to avoid gaps. Is that feasible?
02:20 Maya: Yes, we can align. We'll send a pricing addendum and SOW by next week to sync with your legal.
02:36 Liam: Technical question — what latency SLO are you targeting for EU? P95 under 250ms? 150ms?
02:46 Carlos: Ideally p95 under 200ms for single-turn generation. Multi-turn chat can tolerate a little more.
03:00 Liam: Ok. We'll run a regional bench with your prompt set. We'll test: hosted baseline, dedicated with KV-cache, and dedicated + quantization. Should give token cost and latency tradeoffs.
03:20 Erin: A couple of infra constraints: our infra team requires that the VPC peering supports direct connect and we prefer customer-managed KMS in EU.
03:33 Maya: Understood — private deployment supports customer KMS/HSM and on-prem connectors; VPC peering with direct connect is doable, we just need the networking details.
03:48 Priya: Do you support SAML SSO and granular RBAC for users? We have a broad team of model owners.
04:00 Jiro: Yes SSO via SAML, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC can be scoped per team. We'll map roles with your IdP.
04:12 Carlos: Wanted to raise one concern — last time we saw tail latencies when cache misses hit model variants. Can Redwood route to cheaper variants gracefully?
04:25 Liam: Yes we have smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants. There can be slight quality delta; we'll show tradeoffs in the bench.
04:38 Erin: On cost — can you give an example of cost per effective token for a dedicated pool vs hosted? Our CFO wants concrete numbers for annual budgeting.
04:50 Maya: We'll put three scenarios in the addendum: hosted on current plan, dedicated baseline with reserved GPUs, and dedicated + EU region. We'll show per-token unit economics and committed discount tiers.
05:05 Ben: Also flagging procurement — we may need a short review of indemnities and data residency clauses. Legal will send redlines 1-2 days after they get the SOW.
05:18 Priya: Security follow-up: we need the KMS rotation policy and whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys at rest for logs and KV cache.
05:30 Liam: Short answer: yes for model payloads and KV cache; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM using our log forwarder; KMS rotation details included in the security pack.
05:45 Carlos: Regarding EU onboarding, what's the expected lead time from signature to go-live for an additional region?
05:55 Jiro: Typical runway is 3-6 weeks for EU region provisioning for dedicated — includes infra, network peering, and testing. Private deployments can be longer depending on direct-connect setup.
06:15 Erin: We also want to try a hybrid — start with dedicated hosted EU zone and then move to private VPC if residency is required. Is that a supported path?
06:26 Maya: Yes, you can start hosted/dedicated and transition to private; we support model and version pinning so you won't need to change prompts.
06:38 Carlos: Another important note: we run reranking and embeddings internally. Any guidance on separating embedding workloads to cheaper quantized instances?
06:50 Liam: We recommend moving embedding pipelines to lower-cost quantized endpoints — Optimize has recommendations for quantization per workload. We'll include specific profiles for your embeddings in the bench.
07:05 Ben: One more thing: SLA credits and uptime guarantees for dedicated — can you summarize?
07:13 Jiro: We'll include the dedicated SLA in the addendum; generally 99.9% uptime with credits outlined for region-level failures. Private deployments can be contract-defined.
07:27 Priya: On audit logs — we need forwardable audit trails to our SIEM with at least 180 day retention. Is that standard?
07:38 Maya: We have configurable retention plans; 180 days is available as an add-on. We'll confirm any egress cost for long-term storage.
07:48 Carlos: Ok good. Can we talk timeline? We want to sign before Dec 1 to avoid a coverage gap.
08:00 Maya: That lines up with our internal ops. We'll push the addendum and SOW by Nov 12 so you have time for legal. Benchmarks by Nov 14. Follow-up security call week of Nov 17. Pilot kickoff target Nov 24 if all green.
08:18 Erin: Bench details — for bench can you run: 1) p95 latency, 2) tokens/sec throughput under 100ms, 3) cost per 1M tokens with and without KV cache?
08:31 Liam: Yes to all. Also we'll capture model memory pressure and cold-start behavior for your usage pattern.
08:44 Carlos: Any caveats about KV cache across regions? We worry about cache warming and cross-region costs.
08:54 Liam: KV caches are per-region; cross-region traffic can add RTT and egress. We'll show a warmup plan and prefix caching strategies to reduce cross-region cost.
09:10 Jiro: Operationally we can set autoscale burst policies to handle spikes while protecting baseline commit. That often helps with cost smoothing.
09:24 Ben: On the commercial side, would there be a ramp credit if we commit to a 12-month baseline at 300M tokens?
09:33 Maya: Yes we can structure tiered discounts with a commit. We'll propose a couple of commitment bands in the addendum.
09:45 Priya: A small nit — our legal wants explicit language around customer-managed keys and proof of encryption. Are there existing clauses?
09:55 Maya: We have KMS and HSM integration language; legal can grab from our private deployment appendix. We'll flag that in the doc we send.
10:08 Carlos: Great. Anything on backup/DR for private? If we go private in EU we need DR across two availability zones.
10:20 Jiro: Private deployments can be configured for AZ redundancy; we'll include replication and failover costs.
10:30 Erin: For the bench please include a reproduction script and sample client to run locally so we can validate results ourselves.
10:42 Liam: Will do — we'll include a reproducible harness and a sample prompt set capture that mirrors your production distribution.
10:54 Ben: Procurement timeline reminder — legal will aim to send redlines within 48 hours of SOW.
11:04 Maya: Perfect. Quick check on stakeholders who need to be on the security follow-up — Priya, Erin, and our security lead. Priya you said week of Nov 17 works?
11:14 Priya: Yes mornings CET works best.
11:20 Carlos: Ok final ask — include a short operational runbook for failover behavior in the SOW so our platform team can align.
11:32 Maya: We'll include runbook appendix and a one pager on rollback/fallback behavior.
11:44 Jiro: Anything else from Redwood?
11:50 Liam: Just that we'll try to mimic your peak distribution in bench to ensure cache effectiveness and autoscale thresholds.
12:00 Carlos: Good. Thanks everyone.
12:05 Maya: Thanks all — recap: addendum + SOW by Nov 12, bench results by Nov 14, security follow-up wk of Nov 17, pilot kickoff target Nov 24. Expect docs and links in an email after the call.
12:22 End of recording.
notes: Meeting felt constructive; customer is strongly leaning to committed baseline with EU region add-on. Main blockers are legal redlines and security KMS clarifications. Bench will be decisive for latency commitment.
references: Link: Pricing addendum template (sent after call)
